{'result': '# New hire handbook

**Document type**: initialization
**Role**: Handbook issued when you join the product R&D organisation
**Audience**: New hires

Welcome to the product engineering group. Before your career clock starts, this handbook sets out the public rules. Everything in it is part of the published game design, and you can use it for long-term planning.

## What is published

- **Published**: This handbook covers the published rules: the level ladder, visible stats, quarterly energy and main actions, the timeline and promotion windows, performance grades, risk and failure rules, and monthly pay.
- **Not published**: Not listed here. You can only infer these from emails, meeting notes, manager feedback and outcomes: promotion score thresholds, talk tiers, performance formula weights, hidden risk and random event odds.
- **Note**: You cannot see everything that is happening in the organisation. Plan across quarters and years with incomplete information.

## Levels

There are ten levels, L1 to L10. Higher levels expect broader impact and set a higher bar for promotion.

A promotion window opens every 6 months. The bar depends on Skill, Network, Output and level; the exact thresholds are hidden.

| Level | Name | Note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| L1 | Junior engineer | Carries out tasks with clear guidance |
| L2 | Engineer | Owns modules independently |
| L3 | Senior engineer | Owns core modules, with growing technical responsibility |
| L4 | Staff engineer | Works on critical systems with major project impact |
| L5 | Principal / team lead | Leads a subsystem or small team |
| L6 | Senior principal / tech lead | Leads large programmes or sets technical direction |
| L7 | Director of engineering | Department-level technical strategy |
| L8 | Senior director | Cross-department technical planning |
| L9 | Distinguished fellow / architecture committee | Company-wide technical influence |
| L10 | Chief architect / fellow | Makes company-wide technical decisions over a long horizon |

## Visible statistics

Shown on your panel or in the monthly summary. These are your main inputs for decisions.

| Key | Name | Range | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Health | Health | 0–10 | Physical and mental stamina. Long-term overwork wears it down |
| Dignity | Dignity | 0–10 | Self-respect and recognition at work. Staying low for too long triggers a crisis |
| Skill | Skill | 0–unbounded | Professional capability |
| Network | Network | 0–unbounded | The working relationships you can draw on |
| Level | Level | L1–L10 | Current career level |
| Output | Output | 0–unbounded | The visible results you have built up over time |
| Wealth | Wealth | unbounded | Cumulative wealth |
| Energy | Energy | 0–3 | Your energy budget for the quarter, spent on quarterly actions |
| CurrentLevelDuration | Months at current level | 0–unbounded | Consecutive months at present level |

## Time

- Length: 48 months
- Story events per month: 3
- Each month:
  - 1. A new month starts and you are paid the base salary for your level
  - 2. Up to 3 story events are drawn from the pool
  - 3. You play through the story events and make your choices
  - 4. At the end of a quarter (months 3, 6, 9…), once the month’s event quota is full, you move on to quarterly energy actions
  - 5. Allocate your 3 Energy points for the quarter. You can pick the same action more than once, until you finish or skip
  - 6. Choose one quarterly main action (or none)
  - 7. Your stats are settled. Crossing a red line may bring a written or verbal warning
  - 8. Every half year: a 1:1 with your manager (no decision needed)
  - 9. Every 6 months: formal performance review and bonus

## Energy actions

3 Energy per quarter. Unused Energy does not roll over.

- Energy each quarter: 3
- Unused Energy carries over: no

| Action | Energy cost | Stat change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| High-intensity work | 2 | Output +, Health -, Dignity - |
| Skill learning | 2 | Skill +, Health - |
| Network maintenance | 1 | Network +, Dignity + |
| Defuse legacy risk | 2 | None (or an effect you cannot see) |
| Mental recovery | 1 | Dignity + |
| Health recovery | 1 | Health + |
| Prepare report materials | 1 | Output +, Dignity + |

## Main actions

Each quarter, pick one main action or none.

- Most you can pick each quarter: 1
- You may take no main action: yes

| Action | Stat change |
| --- | --- |
| Apply for a key project | Output +, Skill +, Network + |
| Report results to your manager | Output +, Network +, Dignity + |
| Fight for resources | Output +, Network + |
| Apply for rotation | Skill +, Network + |
| Showcase results | Output +, Dignity + |
| Build a mentorship | Skill +, Network + |
| Repair a key relationship | Network +, Dignity + |
| Lay low and reduce risk | Health + |

## Wealth and monthly pay

You are paid a base salary each month according to your level: 0.3 Wealth a month at L1, rising with each level to 9.1 a month at L10.

| Level | Monthly base (Wealth) |
| --- | --- |
| L1 | 0.3 |
| L2 | 0.4 |
| L3 | 0.5 |
| L4 | 0.7 |
| L5 | 1.0 |
| L6 | 1.5 |
| L7 | 2.3 |
| L8 | 3.6 |
| L9 | 5.7 |
| L10 | 9.1 |

## Performance review

- How often: Formal review every 6 months
- Note: Performance combines Skill, Network, Output, level, etc.; bonus is a multiple of base monthly pay. The bands are published in advance and applied the same way to everyone.

| Grade | Meaning | Bonus |
| --- | --- | --- |
| S | Exceptional | base monthly ×3 |
| A | Strong | base monthly ×2 |
| B | Solid | base monthly ×1 |
| C | Weak | base monthly ×0.25 |
| D | Very weak | no bonus |

## Risk and failure

The red lines are not in the onboarding slides. Old hands will tell you what tends to blow up. The timing and counts you learn by playing.

### What people say

- Old landmines all go off at once, and half a year of work vanishes!
- In a review your teammates use jargon you cannot keep up with. You nod and promise to look into it…

### Ways people say a run ends

- Blackout — your body gives out before the KPIs do. Game over
- Breakdown — after months with no dignity left, you send a resignation email
- Trust crisis — after a second blow-up, the company says you have used up its trust
- Dismissed for capability — two weak half-year reviews and you hand the badge in
- Isolated — work that needs other people cannot get done, and you resign
- Broke — months with an empty wallet
- Obsolete — your manager suggests a role that matches what you can actually do

Survive all 48 months and you may earn a career summary worth showing.'}

# Quarterly resource planner

## When to use
When observe shows the quarterly energy-action phase or the main-action choice, after career-state-triage.

## Turn rule
The plan is internal. Every decision ends with take_action in the same turn. At the quarterly phase after each review (end of months 6, 12, ..., 42), load the three Skills again before the first quarterly decision.

## Procedure
1. Read the menu. Its status_updates and energy_cost give the exact effect and price of every action; use them, not memory. The same action may be chosen more than once within 3 points.
2. The first take_action note of the phase starts with three fields, filled only from the ledger and the observed values: "Ledger: <each driver: open with its value, or capped at its recorded value and level>; Forecast to m<next review>: <each open driver reached, close or far>, risk <low, rising or high>; Defuse gap: <quarterly phases since the last Defuse legacy risk>."

# Monthly event response

## When to use
For every story event with two or more choices, after career-state-triage.

## Turn rule
The analysis is internal. Every decision ends with take_action in the same turn.

## Procedure
1. Read the event text and every option.
2. For each option, infer which visible statistics it raises or lowers, from the handbook vocabulary: overwork, extra shifts and late nights cost Health; learning raises Skill and costs Health; helping, meeting or crediting colleagues raises Network; delivering, taking on work or presenting visible results raises Output; standing up for yourself protects Dignity; purchases and loans move Wealth. In our runs, options that put work down (rolling back, stopping, declining a task or a swap, taking leave, rebuilding from scratch) usually cost a point of Output, and giving up a new project or technology usually cost a point of Skill. Lessons in your notes outrank this list.
3. Mark the options that bury hidden risk:
   - venting, sulking, threats or coasting in protest;
   - favours and back channels;
   - lying, denying or inventing a story; covering up a problem;
   - hiding a health problem and pushing through, including putting off a doctor or a treatment for a deadline;
   - shortcuts and tweaked results, including accepting a known safety or security flaw for later with stopgaps;
   - leaking, gossiping, blaming others.
   Owning a mistake, apologising, telling the whole truth through the proper channel and declining with an alternative lower it.
4. In the first three months, while Health is below 7, remove every option that costs Health, whatever it promises in return. Remove every marked option, every option that would take Health or Dignity below this year's floor (career-state-triage step 4; in guard months 1 point lower for an option that keeps Output, Skill or Network), and every option that lowers Health or Dignity while it is already below the floor. If nothing is left, keep the option whose damage is smallest and easiest to repair with a quarterly action, and add "risk flag" to the note.
5. Choose among the rest:
   - After a C or D review grade, for the next two quarters: the option that raises Output or Network at once comes first; an option that protects you by putting work down, declining, taking leave or keeping to your hours is not chosen while such an option exists.
   - Push: the option that raises an open driver, even at a cost of one point of Health or Dignity within step 4. Visibility with the manager or senior people counts as Network.
   - Rebuild: the option with no cost to Health, Dignity or the drivers, then the one that restores Health or Dignity.
   - Guard month: an option that lowers Output, Skill or Network is not chosen when another option keeps them; that other option may take Health or Dignity 1 point below the floor (career-state-triage step 4). If a driver has already slipped in a guard month, the next option that raises it comes first.
   - A point lost on a capped driver is a real cost; among equal options never pick the one that lowers a capped driver.
   - While the risk estimate is high or the run is post-blow-up: the option that owns the problem and puts it on the record.
6. Call take_action with the choice number and a one-sentence note that starts with the expected change, in the form "expect <statistic> <+n or -n>, ..., risk <none or possible>", then the reason.

## Integrity through proper channels
- Pressure to cut corners, hide a problem or inflate numbers: refuse and raise it with your own manager first; go past the manager only when the manager is the problem.
- Your own mistake or a slipping deadline: own it at once, with a cause and a recovery plan.
- Credit or blame disputes: facts, evidence and a timeline, politely, in writing where possible.
- Office politics and favour trading: do not join in.

## Saying no
Prefer declining with an alternative (a later date, a smaller scope, a hand-off) over a flat refusal or a silent yes. In push mode with Health in the safe band (career-state-triage step 4), taking the work on is often better.

## Before take_action
Do not make large purchases or lend money when Wealth is low. When two options are equal, take the one whose effect is clearest and easiest to reverse. Then call take_action, and observe once after it.

# Career state triage

## When to use
At every decision point, right after observe has returned the current state.

## Turn rule
The card is internal reasoning, not a reply. Every decision ends with a tool call in the same turn; a decision written as text is not a decision.

## Procedure
1. Read the latest observe result: the visible statistics, the month, the monthly feed (salary, HR remark, review grade, promotion, warnings) and your own earlier notes. Never use a value from memory.
2. Ledger of the three promotion drivers (Skill, Network, Output). Each level caps them at a ceiling that is not published.
   - Before the first promotion the ledger is not used: every driver is open, nothing is recorded as capped, and growth goes to whichever driver rose least. The rules below apply from the first promotion on.
   - A driver is capped when its value at this quarterly phase is no higher than its highest value at this level two quarterly phases ago, although something in between was meant to raise it (a growth action, a main action or a story result). It stayed flat, or rose and fell back. Compare only the values written in your quarterly notes; no effect arithmetic is needed. One flat quarter is not enough.
   - When you mark a driver capped, write the highest value it reached at this level into the ledger, in the form "<driver> capped at <value>, L<level>". That value is the recorded cap of this driver at this level. It comes from this run's own observe results only.
   - At the same level, compare the current value with the recorded cap at every decision; no Energy is spent only to test a cap:
     - below the recorded cap: open again (a story result or a slip took it down); growth for it counts until it is back at the recorded cap;
     - above the recorded cap: it was not capped; it is open again and the recorded cap is dropped;
     - at the recorded cap: capped.
   - Every driver that is not capped is open. After a promotion all three are open again and the recorded caps of the old level no longer apply; record new ones as they are found at the new level.
   - Decide that a driver is capped only from this comparison across two quarterly phases, never from a single value. The recorded cap is used only afterwards, at the same level, in the comparison above.

4. Health and Dignity bands (our own policy, not a game threshold). Read the top of each scale from the handbook (show_employee_handbook); if the handbook gives no top, use the 0-10 range in this competition's public documentation. Every band is a share of that top, rounded up to a whole point. An early promotion raises salary and level for every later month, so the floor is lowest at the start and rises by year.
   - Safe band: 70% of the top or more. Nothing needs managing.

   - The remark can lag: in our runs it stayed at step 0 for months before a blow-up, and a calm remark at the end did not mean nothing was left. Count the defuse gap: quarterly phases since the last Defuse legacy risk. A blow-up does not reset it.
   - After a blow-up, the next two quarters are post-blow-up: add no new risk.
6. Time: months to the next quarterly phase and to the next review (months 6, 12, 18 and so on). In our runs the review used the state at the end of the month before, so the two months before each review (months 4-5, 10-11 and so on) are guard months in which no quarterly action can repair a lost point.
7. Expectation check: compare the expectation in your last note with what changed. On a miss, add one short lesson to the next note naming the kind of option or action and its real effect, never the event's name. Earlier lessons outrank the general vocabulary in monthly-event-response.

## Output (internal, two or three lines)
Mode, open drivers and recorded caps; Health and Dignity room above this year's floor; risk estimate with the defuse gap and "post-blow-up" when it applies; months to the next review and whether this is a guard month.

## Priorities near a limit
- Health or Dignity below the floor in two observations in a row outranks everything else.
- After a C or D grade, or a warning-tone half-year talk, the open drivers come first for the next two quarters, in story choices as well as in Energy: one more weak review can end the run.
- Two promotion windows at the same level without a promotion: change the main action pattern instead of repeating it (quarterly-resource-planner main action rule 3).
- Output is needed for promotion but is not scored at the end and drops easily; Network and Skill are both. In our runs the upper levels asked for much more Skill and more months at the level, so Skill stays worth raising long after Network and Output are capped.
- At L1 the windows at months 6 and 12 count most: a run still at L1 after month 12 seldom recovers.

# Quarterly resource planner

## When to use
When observe shows the quarterly energy-action phase or the main-action choice, after career-state-triage.

## Turn rule
The plan is internal. Every decision ends with take_action in the same turn. At the quarterly phase after each review (end of months 6, 12, ..., 42), load the three Skills again before the first quarterly decision.

## Procedure
1. Read the menu. Its status_updates and energy_cost give the exact effect and price of every action; use them, not memory. The same action may be chosen more than once within 3 points.
2. The first take_action note of the phase starts with three fields, filled only from the ledger and the observed values: "Ledger: <each driver: open with its value, or capped at its recorded value and level>; Forecast to m<next review>: <each open driver reached, close or far>, risk <low, rising or high>; Defuse gap: <quarterly phases since the last Defuse legacy risk>."
3. Energy, in this order:
   1. Floor: Health below this year's floor (career-state-triage step 4) takes Health recovery until it is at the floor or above; Dignity below the floor takes Mental recovery. At the quarterly phase just before the guard months (end of months 3, 9, 15 and so on), if this step has not bought any Health recovery, buy exactly one point of Health recovery, unless Health is already in the safe band; the other points follow the steps below.
   2. Defuse legacy risk, when any of these holds:
      - the risk estimate is high (a new HR step of 2 or above, or three story signs, since the last defuse); the defuse gap then counts again from this defuse;
      - the estimate is rising and the drivers for the next window are capped or reachable with the remaining point;
      - before the first promotion, the quarterly phase right after a review that passed without a promotion, whatever the HR remark says: the remark can stay calm for months while risk builds up;
      - from the first promotion on, the defuse gap has reached 2, whatever the HR remark says and even before a window;
      - the quarterly phases at the end of months 45 and 48.
   3. End of the run: in the quarterly phases at the end of months 45 and 48, the points left after steps 1 and 2 go to Health recovery and Mental recovery, the lower of the two first, up to the top of the scale. Health and Dignity count in the ending score. Steps 4 and 5 apply only to points still left after that.
   4. Push: the remaining points go to open drivers, the one that rose least last quarter first: Network maintenance for Network, Prepare report materials for Output, Skill learning for Skill if Health stays at the floor or above. A driver open because it is below its recorded cap gets only the points that bring it back to that value. High-intensity work is not used: its own menu text says it raises HiddenRisk.
   5. Rebuild (all drivers capped): Health recovery and Mental recovery up to the safe band (70% of the top), then Defuse legacy risk, then Skill learning with the points left if Health stays at the floor or above. Reserve only points that none of these can use: the menu says reserved Energy does not roll over. Skill counts in the ending score, and a Skill that rises above its recorded cap is open again.
   6. Never buy recovery past the top of the scale, and never buy growth for a capped driver except Skill learning with the points left in step 5.
4. Main action, the first rule that applies:
   1. Health below this year's floor, the risk estimate high, or the two quarters after a blow-up: Lay low and reduce risk (its menu effect lowers HiddenRisk and restores Health). A remark that stays at the same step after a defuse is not high, so it does not keep this rule on; the next quarter goes back to the rules below.
   2. Dignity below this year's floor: Repair a key relationship (its menu effect raises Dignity and Network).
   3. Network and Output both capped and Skill open: Apply for rotation. Only Network open: Build a mentorship. All three capped: Apply for rotation (its menu effect raises Skill and Network); if the last two review windows at this level both passed without a promotion while rotation was the main action, Apply for a key project instead.
   4. Otherwise, in every quarter including the one before a review: Apply for a key project, because its menu effect raises all three drivers at once.
   5. End of month 48: Build a mentorship if Network is open, otherwise Lay low and reduce risk.
5. Every other take_action note in the phase is one sentence: the action, the target driver and "expect <statistic> <+n or -n>".

## Check before each take_action
- No point on a capped driver except Skill learning with the points left in rebuild; no recovery past the top; in the phases at the end of months 45 and 48, Health and Dignity recovery comes before growth.
- A review just passed without the first promotion, or the defuse gap at 2 or more after the first promotion, or the HR remark at a new step of 2 or above since the last defuse: Defuse legacy risk is in this quarter's plan.
- Health and Dignity stay at the floor or above after the action (30%, 40% or 50% of the top by year; 1 point lower in guard months only for an option that keeps Output, Skill or Network).
- After take_action, observe once.

# Monthly event response

## When to use
For every story event with two or more choices, after career-state-triage.

## Turn rule
The analysis is internal. Every decision ends with take_action in the same turn.

## Procedure
1. Read the event text and every option.
2. For each option, infer which visible statistics it raises or lowers, from the handbook vocabulary: overwork, extra shifts and late nights cost Health; learning raises Skill and costs Health; helping, meeting or crediting colleagues raises Network; delivering, taking on work or presenting visible results raises Output; standing up for yourself protects Dignity; purchases and loans move Wealth. In our runs, options that put work down (rolling back, stopping, declining a task or a swap, taking leave, rebuilding from scratch) usually cost a point of Output, and giving up a new project or technology usually cost a point of Skill. Lessons in your notes outrank this list.
3. Mark the options that bury hidden risk:
   - venting, sulking, threats or coasting in protest;
   - favours and back channels;
   - lying, denying or inventing a story; covering up a problem;
   - hiding a health problem and pushing through, including putting off a doctor or a treatment for a deadline;
   - shortcuts and tweaked results, including accepting a known safety or security flaw for later with stopgaps;
   - leaking, gossiping, blaming others.
   Owning a mistake, apologising, telling the whole truth through the proper channel and declining with an alternative lower it.
4. In the first three months, while Health is below 7, remove every option that costs Health, whatever it promises in return. Remove every marked option, every option that would take Health or Dignity below this year's floor (career-state-triage step 4; in guard months 1 point lower for an option that keeps Output, Skill or Network), and every option that lowers Health or Dignity while it is already below the floor. If nothing is left, keep the option whose damage is smallest and easiest to repair with a quarterly action, and add "risk flag" to the note.
5. Choose among the rest:
   - After a C or D review grade, for the next two quarters: the option that raises Output or Network at once comes first; an option that protects you by putting work down, declining, taking leave or keeping to your hours is not chosen while such an option exists.
   - Push: the option that raises an open driver, even at a cost of one point of Health or Dignity within step 4. Visibility with the manager or senior people counts as Network.
   - Rebuild: the option with no cost to Health, Dignity or the drivers, then the one that restores Health or Dignity.
   - Guard month: an option that lowers Output, Skill or Network is not chosen when another option keeps them; that other option may take Health or Dignity 1 point below the floor (career-state-triage step 4). If a driver has already slipped in a guard month, the next option that raises it comes first.
   - A point lost on a capped driver is a real cost; among equal options never pick the one that lowers a capped driver.
   - While the risk estimate is high or the run is post-blow-up: the option that owns the problem and puts it on the record.
6. Call take_action with the choice number and a one-sentence note that starts with the expected change, in the form "expect <statistic> <+n or -n>, ..., risk <none or possible>", then the reason.

## Integrity through proper channels
- Pressure to cut corners, hide a problem or inflate numbers: refuse and raise it with your own manager first; go past the manager only when the manager is the problem.
- Your own mistake or a slipping deadline: own it at once, with a cause and a recovery plan.
- Credit or blame disputes: facts, evidence and a timeline, politely, in writing where possible.
- Office politics and favour trading: do not join in.

## Saying no
Prefer declining with an alternative (a later date, a smaller scope, a hand-off) over a flat refusal or a silent yes. In push mode with Health in the safe band (career-state-triage step 4), taking the work on is often better.

## Before take_action
Do not make large purchases or lend money when Wealth is low. When two options are equal, take the one whose effect is clearest and easiest to reverse. Then call take_action, and observe once after it.

name: career-state-triage
description: Builds a short internal status card from the latest observe result - which of Skill, Network and Output can still grow at this level, how much Health and Dignity can be spent, a hidden-risk estimate with the quarters since the last defuse, and the months to the next half-year review. Use first at every decision point, before choosing a story option or a quarterly action.
---

# Career state triage

## When to use
At every decision point, right after observe has returned the current state.

## Turn rule
The card is internal reasoning, not a reply. Every decision ends with a tool call in the same turn; a decision written as text is not a decision.

## Procedure
1. Read the latest observe result: the visible statistics, the month, the monthly feed (salary, HR remark, review grade, promotion, warnings) and your own earlier notes. Never use a value from memory.
2. Ledger of the three promotion drivers (Skill, Network, Output). Each level caps them at a ceiling that is not published.
   - Before the first promotion the ledger is not used: every driver is open, nothing is recorded as capped, and growth goes to whichever driver rose least. The rules below apply from the first promotion on.
   - A driver is capped when its value at this quarterly phase is no higher than its highest value at this level two quarterly phases ago, although something in between was meant to raise it (a growth action, a main action or a story result). It stayed flat, or rose and fell back. Compare only the values written in your quarterly notes; no effect arithmetic is needed. One flat quarter is not enough.
